neighbours.label: The word ' so' placed right after an action (a verb or its object) or a noun and leading into what follows from it: purpose or result ('she tied the boat up so it would not drift', 'the boiler failed so the school shut'), and also 'so ADJ that' straight after a noun ('a cliff so steep that'). Strongest with no comma before 'so'. Weak (under about 0.3) for 'so' meaning 'very' after is/was/felt ('the tea is so sweet'), weaker for ', so' after an is/was clause, and quiet for fixed phrases ('if so', 'or so', 'even so', 'and so on', 'so-called') and for the same link made without 'so' ('therefore', 'because', 'in order to').
neighbours.short: ' so' (so that / as a result) right after an action
neighbours.notes: Test sentences written blind by a second author from the label only. Probing: purpose/result 'so' glued to an action read 0.40-0.82, 'so' meaning 'very' after is/was 0.17-0.26, ', so' after a was-ADJ clause 0.13-0.19, fixed phrases 0.02-0.15. Solver (DE) leak: 'Our llama is so fluffy' (0.26 solo, 0.31 assembled). play step ran out of GPU memory; feeder picked from the resident attribution ranking, so no ablation drop was measured.
fire: She tied the boat up so it would not drift away overnight.

Is the ferry late? If so, we walk.

The boiler failed, and therefore the school shut for the rest of the week.
He left the porch light on in order that his sister could find the house.
They built a very high wall, and nobody could see the garden.
We packed extra blankets because the train is always cold.
The road was blocked by a fallen tree; the bus took the long way round.
